concepts.why: Secular scholar, Baptist, Reformed: Col 3:16 says nothing of an assembly; it is about singing in the heart as the word dwells in you, so it shares a theme (song) but not the name, and the same verse already stands in the secondary concept 'Psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs' with Eph 5:19. Drop it from this concept (seven passages remain).

concepts.name: The Holy Spirit given in Acts
concepts.why: Reformed, Lutheran, Baptist and Pentecostal readers would each object, from opposite sides: the name 'They were all filled' is said only by Acts 2:4 and 4:31; Acts 1:5 says 'baptized', 8:17 and 19:6 say 'received' / 'came upon' after hands, 10:44 and 11:15 say 'fell upon'. Under that name the set reads as one repeated experience of 'filling', which is the very point the traditions dispute. A plain label that fits all seven (the passages stay as they are, in canonical order) takes no side.

concepts.name: Women and men among God's people
concepts.why: Secular scholar, egalitarian and complementarian readers alike: 'in the assembly' is not what Joel 2:28, Acts 18:26 (Priscilla and Aquila taking Apollos aside), Acts 21:9 or Phil 4:3 describe; only 1 Cor 11:5, 14:34 and 1 Tim 2:12 are about gatherings. The passages themselves are fairly set (Joel, Priscilla, the four daughters, Phoebe and Philippians 4:3 beside 1 Cor 14:34 and 1 Tim 2:12, whole verses, canonical order) and need no change; only the name says more than half of them.

concepts.name: Guard what has been entrusted to you
concepts.why: Secular scholar, Catholic, Orthodox, Baptist: 'The faith entrusted once for all to the saints' is Jude 3's wording; only Jude 3, 1 Tim 6:20 and 2 Tim 1:14 say anything is entrusted. Acts 17:11 (Bereans examining the Scriptures), Acts 20:30, Gal 1:8, 2 Thess 2:15 and 1 John 4:1 are about testing, false teaching and holding to teaching, and the 'once for all' in the name sets a frame over them, with Acts 17:11 and 2 Thess 2:15 (where readers part on Scripture and tradition) under it. 1 Tim 6:20 ('guard what has been entrusted to you') is the texts' own words that cover the guarding, testing and holding all eight passages do, and keeps Jude 3 and 2 Tim 1:13-14 under it. Passages unchanged.

note_fixes: Acts 10:47: add in place of Colossians 2:12, quoting 'Can anyone withhold the water for baptizing these people, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?' (or the contiguous part of the verse as the BSB gives it)
concepts.why: Baptist, Reformed, Pentecostal (and Lutheran/Catholic for the opposite reason): as now set, the water-and-forgiveness texts lead (Acts 2:38, 22:16, 1 Pet 3:21, Rom 6:4) and the one text where the Spirit is received before the water (Acts 10:47) was dropped for room; the believer-first side is left to Acts 8:38 and Col 2:12. Rom 6:4 and Col 2:12 both carry 'buried with Him in baptism', so one of the two is enough; swapping Col 2:12 for Acts 10:47 restores the passage the traditions cite against each other and still holds 'Acts 16:33' (household) and 'Acts 8:38' (the eunuch) side by side. Name 'Baptism' is a plain label and stays.

secondary_or_links: Possible same-sub-theme pair: 6 'A chosen people, a holy nation' and 7 'Called and chosen' (Deut 7:6 is under 6 and Deut 7:7, the next verse, is under 7; 1 Pet 2:9 'chosen people' and Col 3:12 'the elect' are the same act of God's choosing a people). The drafter splits them as identity versus election and they have different passages, so this is soft; merging would exceed eight passages. Not a required change.
Concepts 41 and 42 (unity / divisions) and 37 (peace) are neighbours but are the two poles and the peace verses, not the same sub-theme; they stand.

Secondary 'Lampstands' and 'Elders and overseers' repeat passages already in concepts 50, 22 and 23; harmless, and the cross-pointing for elders and overseers is a fair way to leave the office question open. No change.
Links: no change. Covenant, Priesthood, Temple/Presence, Spirit, Children of God, Kingdom, Messiah/Christology, Deliverance/Salvation, New Creation are all supported by passages here.

Checked where traditions part and found the outline even-handed: Lord's Supper (bread named as the texts name it, 'This is My body' beside 'a participation' and 'proclaim the Lord's death', the unworthy-manner warning kept); offices (elders, overseers, deacons each in their own words, no word on one office or two); keys (Matt 16:19 beside 18:18 and John 20:23 with no succession claimed); election (Rom 8:30 and Eph 1:4 beside Matt 22:14 and 2 Pet 1:10); Israel and the church (cornerstone, bride, chosen people, far and near and the olive tree all stand OT beside NT with no concept saying one fulfils the other, and Rom 11:22 keeps the warning both ways); the last concept is the theme's own hope and the dark concepts (divisions, expulsion, persecution, Deut 23:3, the letters' warnings) are all left standing.
